CV-03.c01: The **fifth wheel** is the round coupling plate on the tractor; the **kingpin** points down from the trailer, and its middle part is the shank.
The jaws close on the kingpin; the **locking lever** opens them, and a **safety latch** keeps that lever from opening by accident.
**Landing gear** are the two front legs holding up an unhooked trailer, wound with a crank handle.
Trailer air supply knob (red, 8-sided) → **in** = air to the trailer; **out** = trailer air off and trailer emergency brakes on.
CV-03.c02: Getting coupling or uncoupling wrong is **very dangerous**.
The handbook's steps are **general**, because rigs differ, so also learn the details of the truck you will drive.
CV-03.c03: Steps 1–6 → inspect **fifth wheel** (greased, **tilted down toward the rear**, jaws open), inspect area and chock, line up straight, back until it just touches, secure, check height.
Trailer height → **low enough that the tractor lifts it slightly**; too low hits the trailer nose, too high may not couple correctly.
Steps 7–9 before backing under → connect air lines, supply air and check for crossed lines with the **engine off**, then **pull out** the knob to lock trailer brakes.
Steps 10–13 → back under in lowest reverse gear, tug test gently, secure and take the key, then inspect for **no space** between plates and jaws around the kingpin **shank**.
Steps 14–16 → plug in the electrical cord, raise landing gear **all the way up** and secure the crank, check clearances, and finally **remove the chocks**.
CV-03.c04: Park on firm ground with the tractor **in line** with the trailer; lock trailer brakes, **back up gently** to ease jaw pressure, and set parking brakes while pushing.
Chock the trailer wheels if it has **no spring brakes, or you are not sure**, because tank air can leak and let the trailer roll.
Lower the landing gear; on a **loaded** trailer add a few turns in low gear, but **never lift** the trailer off the fifth wheel.
Disconnect air lines onto dummy couplers, hang the electrical cable **plug down**, unlock the fifth wheel, keeping legs clear of the rear tractor wheels.
Pull partly clear and stop with the **tractor frame still under the trailer**, secure, check the ground and landing gear, then pull clear.
CV-03.c05: [CA] These hitches are in the California handbook but rarely tested; know the **safety points** and roughly what each step does.
**Pintle hook**: inspect the hook and mount; it is locked correctly when the lock handle sits **flush with the top of the latch**.
Uncoupling a pintle hook → park on firm, level ground, block the tires, and check the ground can carry the tongue's weight **before** extending the jack.
Ball-type drawbar: back the adjustment screw out at least 5 turns, torque lock screws to **350–400 Nm**, and set a **0.3–0.5 mm** gap.
**Gooseneck**: latch the coupler clamp over a lubricated ball, and hook up **safety chains**, which every trailer must have by law; test every light.
